explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/595 (Erdős–Hajnal): 'Is there an infinite graph G which contains no K_4 and is not the union of countably many triangle-free graphs?'. The Lean statement: ∃ an infinite vertex type V and G : SimpleGraph V with G.CliqueFree 4 and ¬ IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G, where the latter means G = ⨆ i : ℕ, H i for some sequence of 3-clique-free graphs on V (equivalently an ℕ-colouring of the edges with no monochromatic triangle, as proved in the file). 'Countably many' as an ℕ-indexed family loses nothing since ⊥ may be repeated. The universe-polymorphic ∃ (V : Type*) is equivalent across universes via ULift. Stated existentially as an open question. Faithful.
